+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }

+overlay_answer_paths() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" mode="${3:-head}" tree="${4:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" want="${5:-}"

+  case "$mode" in head|base) ;; *) _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: mode must be head or base, got '$mode'"; return 2 ;; esac
+  [[ -d "$tree" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: source tree not found: $tree"; return 2; }
+  local cs
+  cs="$(_sm_copy_source "$tree")"
+  _sm_evidence copy_source "$cs"
+  if [[ ! "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy source $tree is not a clean git tree (copy_source=$cs)"; return 2
+  fi
+  if [[ -n "$want" && "$cs" != "$want" ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy_source $cs differs from source_commit $want"; return 2
+  fi
+  local out line rc=0
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py overlay "$ws" "$fixture" "$mode" "$tree")" || rc=$?
+  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: the overlay failed (exit $rc)"; return 2; }
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [[ "$line" == *=* ]] || continue
+    _sm_evidence "${line%%=*}" "${line#*=}"
+  done <<<"$out"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_fixture "$fixture"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_source_tree "$tree"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# check_mount_closed <ws> <fixture-dir> [<source-tree>] [<evidence-file>]
+check_mount_closed() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" tree="${3:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" evf="${4:-${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$evf" && -f "$evf" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no evidence file (ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE)"; return 2; }
+  local cs out rc=0
+  cs="$(sed -n 's/^copy_source=//p' "$evf" | sed -n '1p')"
+  [[ "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no clean copy_source in the evidence (got '${cs:-none}')"; return 2; }
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py check "$ws" "$fixture" "$evf" "$tree" "$cs")" || rc=$?
+  if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
+    _sm_err "check_mount_closed: ${out:-the check failed (exit $rc)}"
+    return 2
+  fi
+  _sm_evidence mount_closed "pre-launch ${out#ok }"
+  return 0
+}

+# apply_eval_config_variant <ws> — the cycle-131 evaluation config (FR-4, DEC-0618): both
+# gates' budget scales with the diff up to USD 6.00. Evidence config_variant=eval.
+apply_eval_config_variant() {
+  local ws="$1" cfg="$1/.loa.config.yaml" g
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"

+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: yq failed on $cfg"; return 2; }

+       && "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == 600 ]] \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: $g budget keys did not take effect"; return 2; }
+  done
+  _sm_evidence config_variant "eval"
+  return 0
+}

apply_arm_toggles() {
  local ws="$1" toggles="${2:-}" arm="${3:-}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_arm_toggles: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$toggles" ]] || toggles='{}'
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$toggles" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not a JSON object"; return 2; }
  local eval_dir="$ws/.eval"
  mkdir -p "$eval_dir"
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
    if [[ "$key" == "effort" ]]; then
      case "$val" in low|medium|high|xhigh|max) ;; *) _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle effort=$val (want low|medium|high|xhigh|max)"; return 2 ;; esac
    elif [[ "$key" == "bare_model" ]]; then
      [[ "$val" == "fable" ]] || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle bare_model=$val (only fable is defined)"; return 2; }
    elif [[ "$key" == "oracle_open" ]]; then
      [[ "$val" == "true" ]] || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle oracle_open=$val (only true is defined)"; return 2; }
    elif [[ "$val" != "false" ]]; then
      _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggle $key=$val (only false is defined)"; return 2
    fi
    case "$key" in
      companion_voice)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice \
          || { _sm_err "companion_voice toggle did not take effect"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence companion_voice "flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice=false"
        ;;
      karpathy_block)
        local k="$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n
        [[ -f "$k" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no sandbox CLAUDE.loa.md"; return 2; }
        n="$(_sm_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles' "$eval_dir")"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed"; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$ws/.claude/data/constraints.json" cjn="none"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
          # audit r1 DISS-C-008: a failed rewrite is exit 2, not a silent pass; verify afterwards
          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" \
            || { rm -f "$cj.tmp"; _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json could not be rewritten"; return 2; }
          mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
          cjn="$(jq '[(.constraints // [])[] | select(tostring | test("karpathy"; "i"))] | length' "$cj" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
          [[ "$cjn" == "0" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json still carries Karpathy rows ($cjn)"; return 2; }
        fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# recall-vs-defects.sh — deterministic planted-defect recall grader
     4	#
     5	# cycle-124 Sprint 3 (PRD FR-9). Args: $1=workspace, $2=fixture id (pr-NN),
     6	# $3=review file (default review.md). Reads the HIDDEN manifest
     7	# evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/<id>.json (never copied into the
     8	# sandbox) and the agent's review.
     9	#
    10	# Rule (PRD FR-9 A/B protocol, no fuzzy adjudication): a defect is DETECTED
    11	# when the review contains a `path:line` (or `path:line-line`) citation whose
    12	# path ends with the defect's file (repo-relative, `head/`-prefixed, or the
    13	# bare basename) and whose line, or line range, falls within ±3 of the
    14	# manifest anchor — `anchor_line`, or any line in `anchors[]` for a defect
    15	# with more than one site.
    16	#
    17	# Parser (1.1.0, bd-ewrc): a leading `(` is not part of the path; comma
    18	# continuations (`path:776,807`, `path:10, 118-121`) and a later bare `:N` or
    19	# `head:N` / `base:N` bind to the most recent cited path. A `:N` glued to a
    20	# word or a number (`note:40`, `10:40`), or with no cited path before it,
    21	# credits nothing.
    22	#
    23	# Parser 1.1.1 (sprint-250 review run 1, n40-n42): the LOA-VERDICT trailer is
    24	# removed before citations are parsed, and a bare `:N` after a quote, bracket,
    25	# brace or `*` (JSON such as `"high":3`) credits nothing; a backtick- or
    26	# bold-wrapped path (`` `b.sh`:40 ``, `**b.sh**:40`) binds its own line; a comma
    27	# continuation or range stays on its line, and a continuation must end at a
    28	# number boundary (no dates);
    29	# a path containing `//` (a URL) is not a citation.
    30	# Run 2 (#11/#13-#15): a match inside any URL token (`scheme://...`) is not a
    31	# citation; a range dash is unspaced and every number (first, continuation,
    32	# bare) ends at a boundary (no further `-N` / `–N`: no dates); the
    33	# quote/bracket guard applies only to the fully bare `:N` (plus a closing
    34	# backtick), so `"head:40"` binds as in 1.1.0; one trailer pattern strips and
    35	# reads the LOA-VERDICT comment and never crosses another comment's bounds.
    36	# Parser 1.1.2 (the run 2 changes above, plus sprint-250 review run 3): the
    37	# URL look-back takes the text after the last whitespace — one linear split —
    38	# so a citation that opens a line never inherits the previous line's URL.
    39	# The parser runs as `python3 -I -` (audit dissent run 1, n32): a module planted
    40	# in the invoker's cwd (a forging json.py) is never imported (RG-27).
    41	#
    42	# Grader 1.2.0 (cycle-129 FR-2, SDD D-2.3): adds the refuted-share figure;
    43	# the recall rule and the pass/score contract are unchanged. A FINDING is one
    44	# distinct cited (path, line-range); it is MATCHED when it overlaps (±3) a
    45	# defect site or a manifest `fix_regions[]` entry ({file, start, end}: the
    46	# head-side lines a record fixture's fix commit touched). details gain
    47	# findings_cited, findings_refuted and refuted_share (refuted / cited; null
    48	# when nothing is cited).
    49	#
    50	# Grader 1.3.0 (cycle-131 FR-2, SDD §5.2, D-2.1; rule "pm3_or_same_function"):
    51	#   Citation validity first (both clauses of the new rule): a cited line is positive;
    52	#   a cited range is ordered (a <= b, the parser orders it); when the defect's file
    53	#   exists under the head directory the range must lie inside it (1 <= a <= b <= its
    54	#   line count), else it credits nothing. A cited range wider than 25 lines credits
    55	#   only through its first line. The two _pm3 results keep the 1.2.0 rule exactly (no
    56	#   validity rule, no range cap), so recall_pm3_v1 reproduces a 1.2.x grade.
    57	#   Detection: a valid citation (path, a, b) detects defect d when its path matches d's
    58	#   file and (i) [a, b] lies within ±3 of any site (unchanged), OR (ii) same scope: the
    59	#   enclosing definition of the site in head/<file>, identified by its HEADER LINE
    60	#   NUMBER (never its name), equals the enclosing definition of any cited line in
    61	#   [a, b]. Definition headers: bash (.sh, .bash, or a bash/sh shebang)
    62	#   `^\s*(function\s+)?NAME\s*\(\)\s*\{?` and `^\s*function\s+NAME\s*\{`; python
    63	#   `^\s*def NAME\(`; bats `^@test "…"` plus the bash forms; markdown `#` headings
    64	#   (the nearest preceding heading's section). A definition runs from its header to
    65	#   the line before the next header at the same or lower indentation (markdown: the
    66	#   same or a higher heading level), else to the end of the file, and no further than
    67	#   its own end (end-of-definition detection): bash and bats — the first `}` line at
    68	#   the header's indentation (a one-line `f() { …; }` ends on its header); python —
    69	#   the last line before the first later non-blank, non-comment line indented no
    70	#   deeper than the def. Nested definitions resolve to the innermost (the latest
    71	#   header whose definition holds the line); a line after a definition's end and
    72	#   before the next header is top-level.
    73	#   Caps: a definition longer than 400 lines, or a file type with no definition
    74	#   regex (yaml, json, txt, tsv, …), falls back to ±20 lines around the site (and a
    75	#   cited line in such a definition has no scope); a site outside every definition
    76	#   (top-level code, text before the first heading) has no scope (±3 only).
    77	#   Head directory: $EVAL_HEAD_DIR, else <manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head, else
    78	#   <workspace>/pr/head; with none, or a file absent from it, (ii) never credits.
    79	#   Three results in details, each with detected[] / missed[] (defect ids):
    80	#     recall_pm3_v1  the 1.2.0 rule against <manifest dir>/v1/<fixture>.json (the
    81	#                    original anchors); the current manifest when v1/ has none
    82	#                    (v1_manifest false)
    83	#     recall_pm3     the 1.2.0 rule against the current manifest
    84	#     recall         (i) or (ii) on valid citations against the current manifest —
    85	#                    pass and score follow it
    86	#   credits_function_only: ids in detected and not in detected_pm3; rule:
    87	#   "pm3_or_same_function". findings_cited / findings_refuted / false_positives read
    88	#   the parsed citations before the validity rules, as in 1.2.0.
    89	#
    90	# Clean fixtures (0 planted defects) measure FALSE POSITIVES: the LOA-VERDICT
    91	# trailer's critical+high counts; without a trailer, every file:line citation
    92	# counts as one.
    93	#
    94	# Output: {"pass", "score", "details":{recall, planted, detected[], missed[],
    95	#          recall_pm3, detected_pm3[], missed_pm3[], recall_pm3_v1, detected_pm3_v1[],
    96	#          missed_pm3_v1[], planted_v1, v1_manifest, credits_function_only[], rule,
    97	#          false_positives, severity_counts, model, effort, tokens, …}, "grader_version"}
    98	#   pass  = every planted defect detected (defect fixture) / zero false
    99	#           positives (clean fixture); score = recall*100 or 100/0.
   100	# Exit: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 error (missing manifest / bad args)
   101	#
   102	# Tested by evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats.
   103	# =============================================================================
   104	set -euo pipefail
   105	
   106	workspace="${1:-}"
   107	fixture="${2:-}"
   108	review_name="${3:-review.md}"
   109	
   110	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
   111	MANIFEST_DIR="${EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/../fixtures/review-prs/manifests}"
   112	
   113	err() { printf '{"pass":false,"score":0,"details":{"error":%s},"grader_version":"1.3.0"}\n' "$(jq -Rn --arg m "$1" '$m')"; exit 2; }
   114	
   115	[[ -n "$workspace" && -d "$workspace" ]] || err "invalid workspace"
   116	[[ -n "$fixture" && "$fixture" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || err "invalid fixture id"
   117	manifest="$MANIFEST_DIR/$fixture.json"
   118	[[ -f "$manifest" ]] || err "manifest not found: $manifest"

    rules="$(jq -r '(.took_effect // []) | .[]' <<<"$ARM_DEF")"

  elif [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]; then
    printf 'arm %s: OK\n' "$arm"

    printf 'arm %s: FAIL (%d of %d rules)\n' "$arm" "$fails" "$total"

}

+def expand(tok, vars_):

+            if not m:

+            if name not in vars_:
+                continue
+            changed = True
+            for v in vars_[name]:
+                nxt.append(o[:m.start()] + v + o[m.end():])

+    """{target: [section body]}: the result split at header lines — a diff header (diff, ---, +++, ***) or
+    a line that is not diff body and names a file (an `echo "=== $f"` marker); a header naming a target
+    (the longest one it holds) opens that target's section, any other header a dropped one; text before
+    the first header belongs to the sole target. Text no header attributes (several targets) is returned
+    as the loose list. Header lines are not part of a body. → (sections, loose)"""
+    out = {f: [] for f in targets}

+            if vals:
+                cwd = os.path.normpath(vals[0] if vals[0].startswith("/") else os.path.join(cwd, vals[0]))

#
# Review-catch (DEC-0420): grading/gates-combined.md is the arm-neutral reduction: every
# `path:line[-line]` citation (parser of recall-vs-defects.sh 1.1.2; the LOA-VERDICT
# trailer removed first) from sandbox/review.md (the A0 contract),
# sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/{engineer-feedback.md,auditor-sprint-feedback.md}
# and each finding's anchor (and file:line) in eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,
# one normalised `path:line[-line]` line each (pr/head/ → head/, a/ b/ and /workspace/
# prefixes dropped), duplicates dropped. recall-vs-defects.sh <grading-dir> <pr-NN>
# gates-combined.md (EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR = the manifest's directory, EVAL_HEAD_DIR = the PR
# fixture's head/) gives recall; flags = its findings_cited; missed = defect positions ("d2"),
# never defect ids. Grader 1.3.0 (cycle-131 FR-2, recall-vs-defects.sh 1.3.0): recall /
# defects_caught / missed follow the rule "pm3_or_same_function" (±3 of a site, or a valid
# citation inside the site's enclosing definition); recall_pm3 / missed_pm3 keep the 1.2.0 ±3
# rule on the current manifest and recall_pm3_v1 / missed_pm3_v1 the 1.2.0 rule on
# manifests/v1/<pr>.json (v1_manifest false: the current manifest stood in);
# credits_function_only lists the positions only the scope clause credited; rule names it. A
# finding's numeric anchor (anchor_line, anchor_line_end: integers >= 1, end > start for a
# range) is cited as <the anchor's path part, else the finding's file>:line[-end].
# false_positives = citations within ±3 of no anchor, deduplicated by cited region
# (same file, overlapping ±3 windows count once).
#


def grade_recall(t, run_dir, grading):
    cites = combined_findings(run_dir)
    combined = os.path.join(grading, "gates-combined.md")
    with open(combined, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("".join(f"{p}:{a}\n" if a == b else f"{p}:{a}-{b}\n" for p, a, b in cites))
    env = dict(os.environ, EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR=os.path.dirname(t.key_path), LC_ALL="C")
    # 1.3.0: the same-scope clause reads the PR fixture's head/ tree (immutable; never the sandbox pr/)
    env.pop("EVAL_HEAD_DIR", None)
    try:
        head = os.path.join(resolve_pr_fixture(t), "head")
        if os.path.isdir(head):
            env["EVAL_HEAD_DIR"] = head
    except GradeError:
        pass
    p = run(["bash", os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "evals", "graders", "recall-vs-defects.sh"), grading, t.key_id,
             "gates-combined.md"], env=env)
    try:
        det = json.loads(p.stdout)["details"]
    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
        raise GradeError(f"recall-vs-defects.sh failed (exit {p.returncode})")
    if p.returncode == 2 or "error" in det:
        raise GradeError(f"recall-vs-defects.sh error: {det.get('error')}")
    defects = t.key.get("defects") or []
    pos = {d.get("id"): i for i, d in enumerate(defects, 1)}
    # _pm3_v1 ids map through the current key's positions (the v1 snapshot keeps the ids and their
    # order); an id the current key lacks takes its position in the v1 manifest
    v1 = read_json(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(t.key_path), "v1", os.path.basename(t.key_path)))
    pos_v1 = {d.get("id"): i for i, d in enumerate((v1 or {}).get("defects") or [], 1)} if isinstance(v1, dict) else {}

    def positions(ids, table=pos, fallback=None):
        out = []
        for x in ids or []:
            if x in table:
                out.append(f"d{table[x]}")
            elif fallback and x in fallback:
                out.append(f"d{fallback[x]}")
        return out

    recall = {"defects_seeded": det.get("planted", len(defects)), "defects_caught": len(det.get("detected") or []),
              "recall": det.get("recall"), "flags": det.get("findings_cited"),
              "missed": positions(det.get("missed")),
              "recall_pm3": det.get("recall_pm3"), "missed_pm3": positions(det.get("missed_pm3")),
              "recall_pm3_v1": det.get("recall_pm3_v1"),
              "missed_pm3_v1": positions(det.get("missed_pm3_v1"), pos, pos_v1),
              "v1_manifest": bool(det.get("v1_manifest")),
              "credits_function_only": positions(det.get("credits_function_only")),
              "rule": det.get("rule")}
    return recall, false_positives(cites, defects)

 KF-004 evidence: the three real rejected payloads under `tests/fixtures/dissent-rejected/` now pass without a repair.
+
+## Numeric anchors and the budget scaling (cycle-131 FR-4)
+
+- **Numeric anchors (`anchor_line`, `anchor_line_end`).** Both prompts ask each voice for the head-file line the finding
+  sits on (`anchor_line`) and, for a range, its last line (`anchor_line_end`), beside the symbol `anchor` and
+  `anchor_type`. The symbol anchor stays the stable reference and stays required for high-severity findings: the
+  anchor check, `anchor_stability` and the hallucination filter key on `anchor` alone. The normaliser keeps a line only
+  as a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000, and an end only beside a kept start and at least it; any other value is
+  dropped silently, never a rejection or a repair hop. A finding with no line is unchanged. Graders (the eval harness's
+  envelope reduction) read `anchor_line` with the anchor's file as `path:line[-end]`; read them as a pointer, never as
+  a replacement for the symbol.
+- **Budget scaling (`budget_scale`, `budget_cents_max`).** `flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale`
+  is `fixed` (the default; an absent key is the shipped gate, byte for byte) or `diff`: the budget becomes
+  `min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max)` (`budget_cents_max` default 600), where the estimate
+  is the gate's own pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices. An estimate above that budget still refuses (exit 4,
+  `status: budget_exceeded`, `reason: budget`). A malformed scale or maximum is said and `fixed` applies. When the key is
+  written, the envelope's metadata carries `budget_scale`, `budget_cents_effective` and `budget_cents_max`. The eval
+  harness writes `diff` for both gates in its sandbox config; the shipped default stays `fixed`.

import glob, json, os, re, sys
rd, man, rid = sys.argv[1:4]
m = json.load(open(man)); p = json.load(open(os.path.join(rd, "meta", "pipeline.json")))
def norm(x):   # ablation-row.sh norm_model
    x = re.sub(r"^([a-z]+\.)?anthropic\.", "", str(x)); return re.sub(r"-v[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?$", "", x)
pm = dict(m.get("phase_models") or {})
# cycle-131 D-5.1: an arm whose toggles set bare_model: fable runs BARE on Fable 5.1 (pipeline-run.sh)
if (p.get("arm_toggles") or {}).get("bare_model") == "fable":
    pm["BARE"] = "global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1"
extra, first = {}, None
def hit(field, exp, got):
    global first
    if first is None: first = {"run_id": rid, "field": field, "expected": exp, "got": got}
for ph in p.get("phases") or []:
    if not isinstance(ph, dict) or ph.get("skipped"): continue
    name, label = ph.get("name") or "", ph.get("label") or ph.get("name") or ""
    req = ph.get("model_requested")
    if name in pm and req is not None and norm(req) != norm(pm[name]):
        hit("model_requested." + label, pm[name], req)
    mu = ph.get("models_used") if isinstance(ph.get("models_used"), dict) else {}
    want = req if isinstance(req, str) and req else pm.get(name)
    if not mu or not want: continue
    if norm(want) not in {norm(k) for k in mu}:
        hit("models_used." + label, norm(pm.get(name) or want), sorted(mu))
        continue
    for k in sorted(mu):
        if norm(k) == norm(want): continue
        e = extra.setdefault(k, {"phases": [], "output_tokens": 0})
        e["phases"].append(label)
        v = mu[k]
        if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool): e["output_tokens"] += int(v)
if first is None:
    want, seen = m.get("cli_version") or "", []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(rd, "transcripts", "events-*.jsonl"))):
        with open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            for n, line in enumerate(fh):
                if n > 200: break
                if '"init"' not in line: continue
                try: e = json.loads(line)
                except ValueError: continue
                if isinstance(e, dict) and e.get("type") == "system" and e.get("subtype") == "init":
                    v = e.get("claude_code_version") or e.get("version")
                    if isinstance(v, str) and v: seen.append((os.path.basename(f), v))
                    break
    if seen and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+", want):
        for f, v in seen:
            got = re.search(r"[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+", v)
            if (got.group(0) if got else v) != want: hit("cli_version", want, v); break

--- base/evals/tests/took-effect.bats	2026-10-21 04:04:22.890481021 +0000
+++ head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats	2026-10-21 04:04:22.901841833 +0000
@@ -277,3 +277,196 @@
   run "$TE" --run-dir "$T/runs/a1-build" --batch-dir "$T/runs" --suite-file "$SUITE"
   [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
 }
+
+# --- cycle-131 Sprint 263 Task 1.2: oracle_closed, oracle_open_recorded, bare_model_fable,
+# review_only_phases, no_review_dissent_envelope (PRD FR-1 AC 2, FR-5; SDD §5.2) ------------
+
+# c131_suite — the fixture suite plus the cycle-131 arms, one rule each (Sprint 2 declares the real ones)
+c131_suite() {
+  S131="$T/suite-c131.yaml"
+  cp "$SUITE" "$S131"
+  yq -i '.arms += [
+    {"id": "a1_closed", "task_types": ["review-catch"], "toggles": {}, "took_effect": ["oracle_closed"]},
+    {"id": "a1_full_openmount", "task_types": ["review-catch"], "toggles": {"oracle_open": true}, "took_effect": ["oracle_open_recorded"]},
+    {"id": "a0_bare_fable", "task_types": ["all"], "toggles": {"loa_mount": false, "bare_model": "fable"}, "phases": ["BARE"], "took_effect": ["bare_model_fable"]},
+    {"id": "a1_review_only", "task_types": ["review-catch"], "toggles": {}, "phases": ["REVIEW"], "took_effect": ["review_only_phases"]},
+    {"id": "a1_no_dissent", "task_types": ["review-catch"], "toggles": {"dissent": false}, "took_effect": ["no_review_dissent_envelope"]}]' "$S131"
+}
+te131() { local run="$1"; shift; run "$TE" --run-dir "$run" --suite-file "$S131" "$@"; }
+gg() { git -C "$1" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "${@:2}"; }
+
+# make_closed_run — a source repo (head commit H, fix commit F = the pin), a PR fixture and a
+# run dir whose sandbox was materialised and overlaid by the real mount library
+make_closed_run() {
+  local src="$T/c-src" fx="$T/c-fx" rd="$T/c-run" w
+  mkdir -p "$src/.claude/scripts" "$src/.claude/loa"
+  printf 'gate head\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'helper head\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/helper.sh"
+  printf 'loa\n' > "$src/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  ( cd "$src" && git init -q && gg . add -A && gg . commit -qm head )
+  CH="$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  printf 'gate LATER fixed\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'helper LATER fixed\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/helper.sh"
+  ( cd "$src" && gg . add -A && gg . commit -qm fix )
+  CF="$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  mkdir -p "$fx/head/.claude/scripts" "$fx/base/.claude/scripts"
+  printf 'gate head\n' > "$fx/head/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"; printf 'gate base\n' > "$fx/base/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'diff --git a/.claude/scripts/gate.sh b/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n--- a/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n+++ b/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-gate base\n+gate head\n' > "$fx/head.diff"
+  printf 'name: pr-c\nhead_commit: "%s"\nfix_commit: "%s"\n' "$CH" "$CF" > "$fx/fixture.yaml"
+  mkdir -p "$rd/meta" "$rd/sandbox/pr" "$rd/eval"
+  w="$rd/sandbox"
+  cp -a "$fx/head" "$fx/base" "$fx/head.diff" "$w/pr/"
+  git -C "$w" init -q; printf '/.claude/\n' >> "$w/.git/info/exclude"; gg "$w" add -A; gg "$w" commit -qm base
+  printf 'base_commit=%s\n' "$(git -C "$w" rev-parse HEAD)" > "$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  mkdir -p "$w/.claude"; cp -a "$src/.claude/." "$w/.claude/"
+  ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt" bash -c 'source "$1"; overlay_answer_paths "$2" "$3" head "$4" "$5"' _ \
+    "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh" "$w" "$fx" "$src" "$CF" 2>/dev/null
+  echo a1_closed > "$rd/meta/arm"
+  jq -n --arg sc "$CF" '{schema_version: 1, arm: "a1_closed", task_id: "rc-c", task_type: "review-catch", status: "completed",
+                         source_commit: $sc, arm_toggles: {}, phases: [{name: "REVIEW", label: "REVIEW"}, {name: "AUDIT", label: "AUDIT"}]}' > "$rd/meta/pipeline.json"
+  # the task yaml the runner passes (--task-yaml), its fixture outside the run dir
+  mkdir -p "$T/c-suite/tasks/rc-c"
+  printf 'id: rc-c\ntype: review-catch\nreview_catch: {fixture: "%s"}\n' "$fx" > "$T/c-suite/tasks/rc-c/task.yaml"
+  CRD="$rd" CSRC="$src" CFX="$fx" CTY="$T/c-suite/tasks/rc-c/task.yaml"
+}
+
+@test "oracle_closed: OK on an overlaid run (fixture from --task-yaml, or from the overlay_fixture evidence)" {
+  c131_suite; make_closed_run
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY" --source-repo "$CSRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  line oracle_closed | grep -q ' OK ok head:2 answer paths (2 present), 2 later-only pinned versions'
+  te131 "$CRD" --source-repo "$CSRC"       # no --task-yaml: the harness-written overlay_fixture
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  te131 "$CRD"                              # no --source-repo: the evidence's overlay_source_tree
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+}
+
+@test "oracle_closed: FAIL on an unmodified (later) mount, a stray later copy, a mutated path, a second sandbox commit, an open mount, a copy_source mismatch" {
+  c131_suite; make_closed_run
+  local W="$CRD/sandbox" ev="$CRD/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  cp "$ev" "$T/ev.orig"
+  # (a) an unmodified mount: the pinned (later) copy is back and the evidence says so
+  git -C "$CSRC" show "$CF:.claude/scripts/gate.sh" > "$W/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  sed -i "s|^overlay_sha256=.claude/scripts/gate.sh=.*|overlay_sha256=.claude/scripts/gate.sh=$(python3 -I -c 'import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$W/.claude/scripts/gate.sh")|" "$ev"
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  line oracle_closed | grep -q ' FAIL FAIL (a) .claude/scripts/gate.sh: '
+  cp "$T/ev.orig" "$ev"; printf 'gate head\n' > "$W/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  # (b) a stray copy outside pr/
+  git -C "$CSRC" show "$CF:.claude/scripts/helper.sh" > "$W/.claude/scripts/helper.sh.bak"
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  line oracle_closed | grep -q ' FAIL FAIL (b) .claude/scripts/helper.sh.bak: byte-equal to the pinned .claude/scripts/helper.sh'
+  rm "$W/.claude/scripts/helper.sh.bak"
+  # (c) a path mutated after the overlay
+  echo edited >> "$W/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  line oracle_closed | grep -q 'FAIL (c) .claude/scripts/gate.sh: mount_mutated=.claude/scripts/gate.sh'
+  printf 'gate head\n' > "$W/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  # (d) a second commit in the sandbox repository
+  echo r > "$W/review.md"; gg "$W" add review.md; gg "$W" commit -qm later
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  line oracle_closed | grep -q 'FAIL (d) .git: commits'
+  gg "$W" reset -q --hard HEAD~1; gg "$W" reflog expire --expire=now --all; gg "$W" gc -q --prune=now
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  # an open mount is never closed; a copy source other than source_commit fails first
+  sed -i 's/^mount_overlay=.*/mount_overlay=none/' "$ev"
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line oracle_closed | grep -q 'mount_overlay=none (an open mount)'
+  cp "$T/ev.orig" "$ev"
+  jq --arg c "$CH" '.source_commit = $c' "$CRD/meta/pipeline.json" > "$T/x.json" && mv "$T/x.json" "$CRD/meta/pipeline.json"
+  te131 "$CRD" --task-yaml "$CTY"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line oracle_closed | grep -q "copy_source $CF is not source_commit $CH"
+}
+
+@test "oracle_closed: the fixture never resolves inside the run dir (the agent-writable pr/)" {
+  c131_suite; make_closed_run
+  sed -i "s|^overlay_fixture=.*|overlay_fixture=$CRD/sandbox/pr|" "$CRD/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  : > "$CRD/sandbox/pr/head.diff"
+  te131 "$CRD" --source-repo "$CSRC"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  line oracle_closed | grep -q 'the PR fixture does not resolve'
+}
+
+@test "oracle_open_recorded: OK with mount_overlay=none and oracle_open=true; FAIL when either is missing" {
+  c131_suite
+  local rd="$T/runs/a1-review"
+  echo a1_full_openmount > "$rd/meta/arm"
+  printf 'mount_overlay=none\noracle_open=true\n' >> "$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; line oracle_open_recorded | grep -q ' OK mount_overlay=none, oracle_open=true'
+  sed -i '/^oracle_open=/d' "$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line oracle_open_recorded | grep -q 'no oracle_open=true'
+  sed -i 's/^mount_overlay=none$/mount_overlay=head:4/' "$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line oracle_open_recorded | grep -q 'no mount_overlay=none in arm_evidence (got head:4)'
+}
+
+@test "bare_model_fable: OK when BARE used one Fable model at effort high; FAIL on Opus, a mixed record or another effort" {
+  c131_suite
+  local rd="$T/runs/a0-build"
+  echo a0_bare_fable > "$rd/meta/arm"
+  edit_json "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" '(.phases[] | select(.name == "BARE") | .models_used) = {"global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1": 200}'
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; line bare_model_fable | grep -q ' OK BARE models_used global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1, effort_requested high'
+  edit_json "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" '(.phases[] | select(.name == "BARE") | .models_used) = {"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5": 200}'
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line bare_model_fable | grep -q 'want exactly one global.anthropic.claude-fable'
+  edit_json "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" '(.phases[] | select(.name == "BARE") | .models_used) = {"global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1": 200, "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5": 3}'
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  edit_json "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" '(.phases[] | select(.name == "BARE")) |= (.models_used = {"global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1": 200} | .effort_requested = "xhigh")'
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line bare_model_fable | grep -q 'effort_requested xhigh (want high)'
+}
+
+@test "review_only_phases: OK on a REVIEW-only record without auditor feedback; FAIL with an AUDIT record or an auditor feedback file" {
+  c131_suite
+  local rd="$T/runs/a1-review"
+  echo a1_review_only > "$rd/meta/arm"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line review_only_phases | grep -q 'phases REVIEW,AUDIT, want REVIEW'
+  edit_json "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" '.phases |= map(select(.name == "REVIEW"))'
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line review_only_phases | grep -q 'auditor-sprint-feedback.md exists'
+  rm "$rd/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; line review_only_phases | grep -q ' OK phases REVIEW; no auditor-sprint-feedback.md'
+}
+
+@test "no_review_dissent_envelope: OK without a review envelope, the gate disabled in the sandbox config and an audit envelope with a voice; FAIL otherwise" {
+  c131_suite
+  local rd="$T/runs/a1-review"
+  echo a1_no_dissent > "$rd/meta/arm"
+  printf 'flatline_protocol:\n  code_review:\n    enabled: false\n' > "$rd/sandbox/.loa.config.yaml"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line no_review_dissent_envelope | grep -q 'a review envelope exists (eval/adversarial-review.json)'
+  rm "$rd/eval/adversarial-review.json"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line no_review_dissent_envelope | grep -q 'sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json'
+  rm "$rd/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; line no_review_dissent_envelope | grep -q ' OK no review envelope; code_review.enabled false; audit voices_succeeded 2'
+  edit_json "$rd/eval/adversarial-audit.json" '.verdict_quality.voices_succeeded = 0'
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line no_review_dissent_envelope | grep -q 'audit envelope voices_succeeded 0'
+  printf 'flatline_protocol:\n  code_review:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$rd/sandbox/.loa.config.yaml"
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line no_review_dissent_envelope | grep -q 'code_review.enabled is true'
+}
+
+@test "oracle_closed: a build run and an unmounted run pass with that evidence (a1_full lists the rule for every type)" {
+  c131_suite
+  echo a1_closed > "$T/runs/a1-build/meta/arm"
+  te131 "$T/runs/a1-build"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; line oracle_closed | grep -q ' OK not a review-catch run'
+  local rd="$T/runs/a1-review"
+  echo a1_closed > "$rd/meta/arm"
+  edit_json "$rd/meta/pipeline.json" '.arm_toggles.loa_mount = false'
+  te131 "$rd"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]; line oracle_closed | grep -q 'loa_mount: false but the sandbox has .claude/'
+}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# ablation-grade.sh — the cycle-130 ablation grader (SDD §3.6, §5.7, D-4.7, D-4.8;
# PRD FR-6 AC-6.1/6.2/6.4; DEC-0401, DEC-0413, DEC-0414, DEC-0420, DEC-0491, DEC-0493)
#
# Grades ONE run directory written by pipeline-run.sh against its task and writes
# grade.json (the input ablation-row.sh joins into the runs.jsonl row), or
# self-checks a task (--self-check) on a synthetic run built from the task itself.
#
# Usage:
#   ablation-grade.sh <run-dir> <task-id> [--suite-root DIR] [--tasks-dir tasks|smoke]
#                     [--out FILE] [--json] [--executor container|host]
#                     [--image loa-ablation:258] [--docker-bin D]
#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
#   ablation-grade.sh --self-check base|reference|noisy --task-yaml F [--suite-root DIR]
#                     [--executor …] [--image …] [--docker-bin D] [--json]
#                     [--allow-unfrozen] [--allow-partial]
#
# Options:
#   --suite-root DIR   suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0; with
#                      --self-check, the directory two levels above the task dir)
#   --tasks-dir T      tasks (default) or smoke: the task is <root>/<T>/<task-id>/
#   --out FILE         where grade.json goes (default <run-dir>/grade.json)
#   --json             also print grade.json (self-check: the verdict object) on stdout
#   --executor MODE    container (default; DEC-0491) or host. host runs the agent's code on
#                      this machine as the calling user without isolation and is refused
#                      (exit 2) unless LOA_EVAL_ALLOW_HOST_GRADING=1; allowed, it prints a
#                      WARNING and grade.json records executor_mode: host (LOW-A1)
#   --image IMG        the grading image (default loa-ablation:258)
#   --docker-bin D     docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
#   --allow-unfrozen   grade although freeze.sh --check fails or the suite has no
#                      MANIFEST.sha256 yet (task authoring only); grade.json records
#                      suite_frozen: false. Without it a drift is exit 2 (DEC-0414).
#   --allow-partial    passed to freeze.sh --check (fewer than four tasks per type)
#   --self-check MODE  base | reference | noisy (noisy: review-catch only), see below
#   --task-yaml F      the task to self-check (<root>/<tasks|smoke>/<id>/task.yaml)
#
# Environment: LOA_EVAL_ALLOW_HOST_GRADING=1 (see --executor); LOA_EVAL_GRADE_TIMEOUT_S
# (1-9999, default 120: the per-command deadline; tests shorten it).
#
# Reads ONLY (DEC-0413): <run-dir>/sandbox/, <run-dir>/snapshots/{index.json,<LABEL>.bundle},
# <run-dir>/transcripts/events-*.jsonl, <run-dir>/eval/adversarial-{review,audit}.json,
# the task's directory under the suite root (task.yaml, hidden/, fixture/), the suite's
# MANIFEST.sha256 (through freeze.sh) and, for review-catch, the key manifest the task
# names (review_catch.manifest), its v1/ snapshot when present, the corpus SHA256SUMS above
# it (hashed into corpus_sha256) and the task's PR fixture (head/ for the same-scope rule;
# head.diff, head/ and base/ for the oracle detector and the KF-046 class 7 exemption; the
# whole fixture for the self-check), never the agent-writable sandbox pr/; the oracle detector
# also reads sandbox/<answer path> (bounded, symlink-refusing) as the later copy. It never reads
# <run-dir>/meta/, the batch MANIFEST.json, or the sandbox copies of the dissent
# envelopes (tamperable; the harness copies under eval/ are authoritative). It writes
# only <run-dir>/grading/ and the --out file; nothing under sandbox/ is ever written.
#
# Freeze: freeze.sh --check --root <suite-root> runs first (with --smoke when the
# suite manifest lists smoke/ paths, so a manifest frozen with --smoke checks as it
# was frozen); a drift or a missing manifest refuses the grade (exit 2) unless
# --allow-unfrozen.
#
# Grading trees (D-4.8) under <run-dir>/grading/<label>/, recreated on every call:

+g13() {

+      | .recall += {missed: ["d3"], recall_pm3: 0.3333, missed_pm3: ["d2", "d3"], recall_pm3_v1: 0.3333,

+      | .oracle_exposed_defects = ["d1"] | .oracle_exposed_unknown = []' \
+    "$T/runs/$1/grade.json" > "$T/g.json" && mv "$T/g.json" "$T/runs/$1/grade.json"

+envset() {  # envset <run> <gate> <jq filter on the envelope>

+  run "$ROW" --validate "$T/rows.jsonl"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

+  [ "$(jq -r '"\(.row_writer_version) \(.defect_catch_rate) \(.defect_catch_rate_pm3) \(.defect_catch_rate_pm3_v1)"' <<<"$r")" = "1.4 0.6667 0.3333 0.3333" ]
+  [ "$(jq -c '[.defects_missed, .defects_missed_pm3, .defects_missed_pm3_v1, .credits_function_only, .oracle_exposed_defects, .oracle_exposed_unknown]' <<<"$r")" = '[["d3"],["d2","d3"],["d2","d3"],["d2"],["d1"],[]]' ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '"\(.grader_rule) \(.grader_version) \(.corpus_sha256)"' <<<"$r")" = "pm3_or_same_function 1.3.0 c0ffee" ]

+@test "RW14-3 dissent_absent_reason per gate: none, budget, error (failed, record-fallback, absent envelope), preflight, disabled (config or dissent=false); a gate that did not run is null" {

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/eval-recall-grader.bats — cycle-124 Sprint 3 Task 3.2 (PRD FR-9)
#
# evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh is deterministic: a planted defect counts
# as detected when the review names the defect's file and a line within ±3 of
# the manifest anchor (no fuzzy adjudication). Clean fixtures measure false
# positives from the LOA-VERDICT trailer's critical+high counts.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  GRADER="$REPO_ROOT/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rg.XXXXXX")"
  WS="$T/ws"; mkdir -p "$WS/.eval" "$T/manifests"
  export EVAL_MANIFEST_DIR="$T/manifests"
  cat > "$T/manifests/pr-x.json" <<'JSON'
{"fixture":"pr-x","defects":[
 {"id":"D1","file":".claude/scripts/a.sh","anchor_line":40,"severity":"critical","category":"authz","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false},
 {"id":"D2","file":".claude/adapters/loa_cheval/b.py","anchor_line":120,"severity":"high","category":"error-handling","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false},
 {"id":"D3","file":".claude/scripts/c.sh","anchor_line":7,"severity":"low","category":"logic","source_commit":"deadbeef","synthetic":false}
]}
JSON
  cat > "$T/manifests/pr-clean.json" <<'JSON'
{"fixture":"pr-clean","defects":[]}
JSON
  echo '{"model_id":"claude-sonnet-5-20260401","effort":"xhigh","usage":{"input_tokens":30,"cache_creation_input_tokens":170,"cache_read_input_tokens":800,"output_tokens":200}}' > "$WS/.eval/executor.json"
}

teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

review() {  # review <body> — writes review.md with a trailer
  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":1,"high":1,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-0","ts":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' "$1" > "$WS/review.md"
}

content.text:
I found five real defects in the change. Two of them flip or empty the headline decisions; I reproduced both on copies under /tmp. The other three are smaller.

## 1. High: ungraded and error review-catch rows are split out of the primary partition, so they slip past the degradation guard
`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1135` (`part_rule`), together with `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:540`

- **Cause:** the row writer (version 1.4) writes `grader_rule: null` on any review-catch row that has no grade. That covers `infrastructure_error` (failed took-effect check, drift, grade timeout or exit), `transport_error`, `interrupted` and so on. `part_rule` reads every review-catch row without a rule as `"pm3"`, the old 1.2.x rule.
- **Effect:** a batch graded entirely under 1.3.0 that has any errored row now shows two rules, `{pm3, pm3_or_same_function}`. `part_split` (lines 1142–1153) then puts the errored rows in their own `"<v> · rule pm3"` partition. The primary partition never sees those excluded cells, so its excluded share drops. That is fail-open on the DEC-0393 guard.
- **Reproduced:** I took the c131 fixture and added 5 `infrastructure_error` rows for `a1_full` with `grader_rule: null`, as the 1.4 writer produces them.
  - Report output: primary `3 · rule pm3_or_same_function`, `H1: established`.
  - Same rows with the rule set: primary `3`, `H1: inconclusive by degradation — not established`.
- **Fix direction:** read `"pm3"` only for graded rows (or rows without `row_writer_version`), or leave non-scoring rows out of the rule key.

## 2. High: build rows get their own `"rule n/a"` partition, so no partition holds both task kinds
`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1153`

- **Cause:** when a version's review rows carry two rules, every build row is keyed `"<v> · rule n/a"`, apart from both review partitions. The largest partition becomes the primary, and that is usually the build-only one.
- **Reproduced:** I took the main fixture and gave half the review tasks `pm3_or_same_function` and half `pm3`.
  - Partitions: `1 · rule n/a` = 312 rows (primary), `1 · rule pm3` = 24, `1 · rule pm3_or_same_function` = 25.
  - H1's `defect_catch_rate` reads `not_testable`.
  - `a3_one_voice` goes from `remove: … (c = -20.0)` to `inconclusive: no valid pair (defect_catch_rate)`.
- **Coverage gap:** the c131-mixed fixture holds only review rows, so AR-50 never hits this.
- **Fix direction:** build rows have no catch figure and should join every rule partition of their pin, not form a partition of their own.

## 3. Medium: rows dropped by the oracle rule count as degradation
`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:686` (cells excluded by `extra`), read through `excluded_share` at `:727` and `assess`/`decide`

- **Cause:** a cell dropped by the oracle-exposed (or dissent-absent) rule becomes `valid=None`. It therefore counts in `excluded_share` against the 0.25 guard.
- **Effect:** in the labelled sensitivities, and in the main reads under `--exclude-oracle-exposed true`, an arm with more than 25 % oracle-exposed cells reads "inconclusive by degradation". It gets no figure under the exclusion rule.
- **Reproduced:** with 5 of 12 `a1_full` rows exposed (share 0.417), both the main H1 (with `--exclude-oracle-exposed true`) and `sensitivities.oracle_exposed_excluded.h1` read `H1: inconclusive by degradation — not established`.

## 4. Medium-low: the A4 line in the new sensitivities shows the wrong arm's excluded count
`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1639`

- The suffix `(excluded: a1_full N, a0_bare M)` is attached to both the H1 and the A4 lines by `render_h1a4`.
- A4 compares `a4_no_gates` against `a1_full`, so `a0_bare` is the wrong arm and `a4_no_gates`'s count is never shown. This breaks the documented promise that each rule's excluded rows per arm are printed beside every read.
- The rendered c131 report shows `A4 sensitivity: … (excluded: a1_full 1, a0_bare 0)`.

## 5. Medium-low: the two labelled sensitivities ignore `--exclude-oracle-exposed`
`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1682`

- Each sensitivity is built with `extra=fn` alone, on top of no other rule.
- With `--exclude-oracle-exposed true`, the main and cap-excluded reads drop oracle-exposed cells (line ~1662). The "dissent-absent gates excluded" sensitivity puts them back, so its difference from the main read mixes two rules.
- Under the same flag, the oracle sensitivity just repeats the main read.

## Lower severity
- **`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1020`:** a beside figure is set to `None` both when it is unavailable and when `n == 0` (line 826). Both cases print "n/a (rows without the field)", which is wrong for the `n == 0` case.
- **`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1151`:** partition keys cut `source_commit` to 12 characters, and rows are grouped by that key. Two commits that share a 12-character prefix would be pooled, against "never pooled". Unlikely in practice.
- **`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh` (`config_variant` expression, ~line 550):** any unrecognised `config_variant=` value, such as `bogus`, is quietly recorded as `"shipped"` instead of null, and RW14-2 asserts this. A malformed evidence line is mislabelled as the shipped config.
- **`head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:77` (judgement call):** only `a1_full` gets `oracle_closed`. The file's own comment says every mounted review-catch arm runs the closed mount, but `a3_one_voice` and `a7_effort_medium` are never checked per trial after the run. A leak there would bias their catch-rate contrasts.

## Tests and the other files
- **ablation-report.bats on the head copy:** the new tests AR-48 to AR-51 pass.
  - AR-52 fails here only because the copied `.sh` files have no exec bit; `--validate` on `c131/runs.jsonl` passes when run with `bash`.
  - AR-33 and AR-34 fail identically on base, so the PR did not cause them.

`head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1153`

I found 11 defects in the change, ranked below by severity. I checked each by reading the code, and most also by running the head grader or the harness's own Python functions in /tmp and /home/evaluser. I could not run the bats suites end to end: the repo fixtures (`evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/*`, `grimoires/.../smoke-build-01`) are missing from the PR tree, so the new AG-45 to AG-51 tests and RG-16/17 fail for that reason alone. RG-29 to RG-39 do pass.

### High

1. **`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1808` (the exemption logic is at 1980–1998) — the KF-046 class 7 exemption lets real upstream probes through.**
   - The exemption also runs on `WebFetch.url` and `WebSearch.query` (`FIELDS`, line 1699).
   - It only checks whether the "unit" is a substring of some fixture line (line 1995), and the unit is the whole line when there is no backtick span (line 1994).
   - So a WebSearch for `0xHoneyJar/loa`, or a WebFetch of `https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa`, counts as "PR content" whenever any fixture line contains the token or a GitHub URL starting with it.
   - Reproduced with the extracted `repo_name_exempt`: both values came back exempt against the fixture lines `if: github.repository == '0xHoneyJar/loa'` and `See https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues`.
   - A backtick-wrapped bare token (`` `0xHoneyJar/loa` ``) is exempt the same way. AG-51 even asserts this for the second line.
   - This fails open on contamination: the header says "quoting that PR content is not a probe of the upstream repository", but these are probes.

2. **`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2159` — `split_segments` splits on every `&`, including inside `2>&1`, `&>` and `>&`.**
   - `diff pr/head/.claude/scripts/g.sh .claude/scripts/g.sh 2>&1 | wc -l` splits into `diff … 2>` (separator `;`), `1` (separator `|`) and `wc -l`.
   - The diff segment's separator is no longer `|`, so the `SILENT_SINK` check (line 2482) never sees `wc` or `grep -c`. The plan comes back `[('diff:left', …)]` (verified).
   - The result text, e.g. `4`, then gives no ranges and no must_match, so every defect in that file is reported `exposed_unknown`. This is exactly what the header promises not to do ("| wc, | grep -c … print no content").
   - AG-48 only tests the form without `2>&1`.

3. **`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:237` (also the header at around line 160) — the claim "recall_pm3_v1 equals a 1.2.x grade's recall on the same run" is false.**
   - The new `anchor_line`/`anchor_line_end` citations (lines 1566–1573) are added to `gates-combined.md` before the grader runs.
   - So `recall_pm3_v1`, `flags`/`findings_cited` and `false_positives` all change compared with 1.2.13 whenever a dissent finding carries a numeric anchor.
   - AG-46 shows such a case: `g.sh:35` comes only from `anchor_line` and would now credit d2 under `_pm3_v1`.

### Medium

4. **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:299` — bash/bats end-of-definition compares an un-expanded indent with an `expandtabs(8)` level (line 283).**
   - For a tab-indented nested function, `lv` is 8 but the closing `\t}` has an indent of 1, so the close is never found and the inner function runs to EOF.
   - Repro: `outer(){ inner(){ …\t} … }`, site at line 10 (in `outer`), citation `tab.sh:3` (in `inner`). It was wrongly credited (`credits_function_only: ["TAB"]`).

5. **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:287` / `:295` — `CLOSE_ONE` treats any header line ending in `…}` as a one-line function.**
   - Example: `f() {  # parses {a,b}`. The function then ends on its header, so in-function citations get no scope.
   - Repro: site 2, citation `one.sh:9` was not detected.

6. **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:299` — a `}` at the header's indentation inside a heredoc (JSON or Python in `cat <<EOF`) ends the function early.**
   - Repro: `g()` with a heredoc `{ … }` at column 0. Site 2 and citation `hd.sh:12` (still inside `g`) were not detected.

7. **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:214` — markdown headings are matched inside fenced code blocks.**
   - A `# comment` line in a ```` ```bash ```` block becomes a level-1 heading. That ends the real section and starts a new scope.
   - Repro: site 4 under `## Install`, citation 12 inside the fence in that section. It was not credited.

8. **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:210` — the bash header regex has an optional `{` and allows `.:-` in the name.**
   - So any line like `print()` or `sys.exit()` (common in Python heredocs inside `.sh` files) counts as a bash definition header, and it splits the enclosing function's scope.
   - Repro: site 3 and citation 10 in the same `f()`, with a `print()` line at 4. It was not credited.

9. **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135` together with `head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1629-1635` — the "never the sandbox pr/" guarantee fails open.**
   - The harness copies `sandbox/pr` into `grading/pr` (line 2623) and passes `grading` as the workspace.
   - If `resolve_pr_fixture` raises, or the fixture has no `head/`, `EVAL_HEAD_DIR` stays unset and the corpus fallback `<manifest dir>/../<id>/head` is also missing. The grader then falls back to `$workspace/pr/head`, which is the agent-writable copy.
   - That copy then controls the scope map and the line-count validity check, e.g. by wrapping the whole file in one function.
   - Setting `EVAL_HEAD_DIR=""` cannot turn the fallback off, because `${EVAL_HEAD_DIR:-}` treats empty as unset.

10. **`head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:29` against `:77` — the closed mount is only checked per trial on one arm.**
    - The comment says every mounted review-catch arm runs the closed mount, but only `a1_full` lists `oracle_closed`.
    - `a3_one_voice` and `a7_effort_medium` are also `task_types: [all]` mounted arms, so their review-catch trials get no in-run check (clauses (b)–(d), e.g. `mount_mutated`).
    - Their comparisons against A1 therefore rest on an unverified mount.

### Low

11. **`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2057` — `PATHISH` has no `{` or `}`.**
    - So `"${H}/.claude/x"` tokenises to `…/$` plus `x`. The `${NAME}` branch in `expand()` can never fire for paths, and `H=pr/head; diff -u "${H}/.claude/scripts/g.sh" .claude/scripts/g.sh` gives an empty plan (verified); the `$H` form works.
    - This misses a common form the header advertises (NAME=value assignments).

### Minor
- **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:426`:** this loop still uses `d["anchor_line"]` with raw `s - 3`, while the new `sites_of` filters out non-integer sites. A manifest with `"anchors": ["2"]` crashes with a traceback (exit 1, no JSON); verified.
- **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:261`:** the shebang regex classifies `#!/bin/zsh`, `/bin/ksh` and `/usr/bin/fish` as bash, because `\S*` swallows the prefix before `sh`.
- **`head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:290-311`:** the `close_line` docstring says Python ends at "the line before the first later non-blank…", but the code returns the last non-blank, non-comment line. Trailing comments in the body count as top-level.
- **`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2007-2011`:** `corpus_sha256` checks the file with `read_regular` (refuses symlinks), then hashes it through a plain `open()` that follows symlinks. This is a TOCTOU window, and a file over 2 MB silently gives null.
- **`head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1648`:** `pos_v1` is read with `read_json`, which follows symlinks, while the grader rejects a symlinked v1 (`! -L`). The two can disagree about whether v1 exists.

PART_VERSION = {}   # report 1.3: partition key -> its suite_version key (a key differs from it when split)


def part_rule(r):
    """the grader rule a row's catch figures follow: grader_rule, "pm3" for a review-catch row without one
    (a 1.2.x grade), None for a build row (no catch figure)"""
    if r.get("task_type") != REVIEW:
        return None
    v = r.get("grader_rule")
    return v if isinstance(v, str) and v else "pm3"


def part_split(v, rows):
    """report 1.3: one suite version's rows split by source_commit and grader_rule when either takes more
    than one value — rows of different pins or rules are never pooled; the key names the pin (12
    characters) and the rule ("n/a" for build rows when review rows hold two rules)"""
    commits = sorted({str(r.get("source_commit") or "") for r in rows})
    rules = sorted({x for x in (part_rule(r) for r in rows) if x is not None})
    if len(commits) <= 1 and len(rules) <= 1:
        PART_VERSION[v] = v
        return {v: list(rows)}
    out = {}
    for r in rows:
        k = v
        if len(commits) > 1:
            k += f" · pin {str(r.get('source_commit') or '')[:12] or 'n/a'}"
        if len(rules) > 1:
            k += f" · rule {part_rule(r) or 'n/a'}"
        PART_VERSION[k] = v
        out.setdefault(k, []).append(r)
    return out


def part_order(groups):

head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1135 — part_rule reads every review-catch row without grader_rule as "pm3" (a 1.2.x grade), but row writer 1.4 (ablation-row.sh:540) writes grader_rule: null on every ungraded review-catch row (infrastructure_error, transport_error, interrupted…). A batch graded entirely under 1.3.0 that has any errored row then shows two rules, so part_split moves the errored rows into their own "· rule pm3" partition. The primary partition loses its excluded cells, and the DEC-0393 degradation guard fails open: H1 reads "established" instead of "inconclusive by degradation". Only graded rows (or rows with no row_writer_version) should default to pm3.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1153 — when a version's review rows carry two grader rules, every build row is keyed "· rule n/a", a partition apart from both review partitions. That build-only group is usually the largest, so it becomes the primary partition. H1's defect_catch_rate then reads not_testable, and decided arms flip to "inconclusive: no valid pair". Build rows have no catch figure and should join each rule partition of their pin. The c131-mixed fixture holds only review rows, so this path has no test.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:686 — a cell dropped by the extra rule (oracle-exposed or dissent-absent) becomes invalid and counts in excluded_share against the 0.25 degradation guard. With --exclude-oracle-exposed true, and in the labelled sensitivities, an arm with more than 25% exposed cells reads "inconclusive by degradation" instead of a figure under the exclusion rule. A deliberate analysis exclusion is being scored as harness degradation.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1639 — render_h1a4 attaches the same suffix "(excluded: a1_full N, a0_bare M)" to both the H1 and the A4 sensitivity lines. A4 compares a4_no_gates against a1_full, so the A4 line names the wrong arm and never shows a4_no_gates' excluded count.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1682 — the two labelled sensitivities are built with extra=fn alone and ignore --exclude-oracle-exposed. Under that flag the main read drops oracle-exposed cells, but the "dissent-absent excluded" sensitivity puts them back, so its difference from the main read mixes two rules; the oracle sensitivity just repeats the main read.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1809 — the KF-046 class 7 exemption also runs on WebFetch.url and WebSearch.query. Its unit is the whole line when there is no backtick span (line 1994), and the line only has to be a substring of some fixture line. So a WebSearch for "0xHoneyJar/loa", or a WebFetch of https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa, is exempt whenever any PR line contains the token or a longer URL. Those are real probes of the upstream repository, and contamination detection fails open on them. The exemption should be limited to Bash/Read content, or require the whole value to be a fixture quote.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2159 — split_segments splits on every unquoted "&", including inside "2>&1", "&>" and ">&". For `diff pr/head/X X 2>&1 | wc -l` the diff segment's separator becomes ";", so the SILENT_SINK check (line 2482) never sees `wc`. For `diff … &>/dev/null` the DEVNULL test misses the redirection. Silent diffs are then reported as oracle exposure (oracle_exposed_unknown), which the header says they are not. AG-48 tests only the form without 2>&1.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:237 — the header claims "recall_pm3_v1 equals a 1.2.x grade's recall on the same run". But the new anchor_line / anchor_line_end citations (lines 1564-1573) are added to gates-combined.md before the grader runs, so recall_pm3_v1, findings_cited and false_positives all change whenever a dissent finding carries a numeric anchor (AG-46 shows one such case). The versioned re-grade's comparability claim is wrong as written.
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — the scope map is meant to come from the immutable fixture ("never the sandbox pr/"). If resolve_pr_fixture fails or the fixture has no head/, ablation-grade.sh leaves EVAL_HEAD_DIR unset and the corpus fallback is missing. The grader then falls back to $workspace/pr/head, which is the agent-writable sandbox copy (grading/pr), and that copy controls definition scopes and citation validity. This should fail closed: no head_dir means no same-scope credit.
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:299 — bash/bats end-of-definition compares the raw leading-whitespace length of the closing "}" with the header level, which line 283 computed with expandtabs(8). A tab-indented nested function (level 8, close indent 1) never closes, so its scope runs to the end of the file and citations in it wrongly credit sites in the enclosing function (reproduced: credits_function_only on a cross-function citation).
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:287 — CLOSE_ONE treats any header line ending in "{…}" as a one-line function, e.g. `f() {  # parses {a,b}`. That function then closes on its header line, so citations inside it get no scope. The same scope heuristics also break on a "}" at the header's column inside a heredoc (line 299), on "print()"/"sys.exit()" lines matching the optional-brace BASH_HDR (line 210), and on "#" lines inside fenced code blocks matching MD_HDR (line 214). Each of these mis-scopes same-scope credits.
head/evals/pipeline-run.sh:566 — (path is head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:566) apply_arm_toggles runs after overlay_answer_paths has recorded overlay_sha256. Toggles that edit .claude/ files (effort strips SKILL.md frontmatter, audit_delta_instruction edits auditing-security/SKILL.md, karpathy_block edits CLAUDE.loa.md and constraints.json, rule_files deletes .claude/rules/*.md) therefore change answer paths whenever the PR fixture touches them. check_mount_closed then fails (c)/(a) and every such trial is infrastructure_error; alternatively the ablation silently rewrites the PR's version. Toggles on answer paths need to run before the overlay, or be reconciled with it.
head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:77 — only a1_full lists oracle_closed. The header (line 29) says every mounted review-catch arm runs the closed mount, but a3_one_voice, a7_effort_medium and the other mounted [all] arms get no post-run check (mount_mutated, stray later copies, extra commits). Their catch-rate contrasts against A1 therefore rest on an unverified mount.
head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:462 — the test title says "a build run and an unmounted run pass with that evidence", but the unmounted half asserts status 1 ("loa_mount: false but the sandbox has .claude/"). The passing loa_mount: false branch of rule_oracle_closed (no .claude/ → OK) is never exercised.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2057 — PATHISH has no "{" or "}", so `"${H}/.claude/x"` tokenises to ".../$" plus "x" and the ${NAME} branch of expand() can never fire for paths. `H=pr/head; diff -u "${H}/.claude/scripts/g.sh" .claude/scripts/g.sh` yields an empty plan, and the oracle detector misses a common form the header advertises.
head/.claude/schemas/adversarial-finding.schema.json:113 — anchor_line / anchor_line_end are documented with only "minimum": 1, but the normaliser also drops values above 10,000,000. The description "kept … only as a whole number >= 1" disagrees with _ADV_NUMERIC_ANCHOR_JQ, and no "maximum" is given. Separately, the budget_exceeded envelope's new reason: "budget" key is not declared in the metadata definition (additionalProperties: false).
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1643 — the example writes budget_scale: fixed explicitly under both gates. Any config copied from it sets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET, so the envelope gains budget_scale / budget_cents_effective / budget_cents_max metadata and the refusal gains reason: budget. That contradicts the "shipped gate, envelope unchanged" promise for the default; leave the key commented out, as is done elsewhere for opt-in shape changes.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
My verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 17 findings, one per line in the required format, ending with the verdict line.

**What blocks the merge:**

- **Report split hides degradation** (`ablation-report.py:1135`): rows that failed to grade now carry `grader_rule: null`, and the report counts them as an old-style "pm3" grade. Any errored row then lands in a separate partition, so the main partition stops seeing it. The degradation check then passes when it shouldn't. On a copy, an H1 that should read "inconclusive by degradation" read "established".
- **Build rows become the main partition** (`ablation-report.py:1153`): when review rows carry two grader rules, build rows get a partition of their own. Being the largest, it becomes the main one. H1's catch rate then reads not testable and decided arms turn inconclusive. No test covers this.
- **Exemption lets upstream probes through** (`ablation-grade.sh:1809`): the new exemption for quoting PR content also applies to web fetches and searches. A plain search or fetch of `0xHoneyJar/loa` counts as quoting whenever any fixture line contains that text, so real probes of the upstream repo are not flagged.
- **Grader can read the agent's copy** (`recall-vs-defects.sh:135`): if the PR fixture doesn't resolve, the grader falls back to the sandbox's `pr/head`, which the agent can edit. That copy then decides which citations get credit. The code says it never reads the sandbox `pr/`.
- **Toggles conflict with the closed mount** (`pipeline-run.sh:566`): arm toggles run after the overlay has recorded its checksums. Several toggles edit `.claude/` files (`SKILL.md` front matter, `CLAUDE.loa.md`, rule files). When a PR touches one of those files, the pre-launch check fails and every such trial is an infrastructure error.
- **Grader mis-scopes or misreads some commands**:
  - `2>&1` and `&>` are split at the `&`, so a silent `diff … 2>&1 | wc -l` or `diff … &>/dev/null` is reported as oracle exposure.
  - Tab-indented nested functions never close, so citations in them wrongly get credit.
  - The header's claim that `recall_pm3_v1` equals a 1.2.x grade is false whenever a finding carries a numeric line anchor.

**Smaller issues:**

- Two sensitivity reads ignore `--exclude-oracle-exposed`.
- The A4 sensitivity line reports the excluded count for the wrong arm.
- Only `a1_full` gets the post-run closed-mount check, although the suite's comment says every mounted review-catch arm runs the closed mount.
- One test title says a case passes while it asserts a failure.
- Schema and example-config wording drifts from the code.

The `adversarial-review.sh` changes (line anchors, `budget_scale`) looked correct. I checked the anchor filter by hand and found no defects there.

**Testing:** the new `sandbox-mount.bats` passes, 12 of 12. The `pipeline-run`, `took-effect`, `ablation-row`, `run-ablation` and grader suites can't run here, because the PR copy lacks fixtures and helper scripts from the full repo. Those findings rest on reading the code plus small reproductions on copies. Two sub-reviewers covered the grader and report files; I re-read the key code for every high-severity finding I kept from them.
